data.title: specific location description posted to followers' dashboard for obscured observations!
data.body:
user Jtuttle found a major 'hole' in geoprivacy...

from their post on http://www.inaturalist.org/posts/6518-a-new-way-to-add-observations#activity_comment_548803:

_the locational privacy issue I'm referring to is this: For anyone I follow, when she/he posts several observations with location obscured or private, the _actual_ locations, down to the address and/or coordinates, are listed beneath the set of observations in my dashboard. So I have to assume that this is occurring with others for _my_ obscured/private observations as well. For example, if my husband uses the app (and probably also the website) to upload observations made at our home address, even if he has made the location obscured or private, our home address will display underneath his observations in my dashboard (e.g., "See whiteoak's observations from {FULL ADDRESS}...")! When I go to individual observations, the location is obscured or blocked, but the location information is still right there on my dashboard. If I upload obscured or private observations via the website and enter my own location name (e.g., "Chatham County", but not otherwise overriding the coordinates pulled from the photo), I _think_ it gets around this issue, but I'm not really sure of that._

I just checked this and it is true. it doesn't show the address when i look but does show the street name. See screenshot below:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/7171475/16275330/8e8f4dfc-3877-11e6-8373-5cc0f2c2547c.png)

here's the observation:

http://www.inaturalist.org/observations/3493779

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/7171475/16275383/c47378da-3877-11e6-95af-0631b7d2f631.png)

I just checked by viewing my account from a different account and it is true for observations I've made and obscured at my home as well. In this case it doesn't matter because I literally live on 'main street' of a state capital (albeit a small one) and that is all it says for mine, so not a big deal there. But for a small, short street it could be a much bigger issue.
